Page 1/16 Abstract Due to the inevitable deviation of the casting process, the dimensional error of the turbine blade is introduced

After machining experiments, the maximum position deviation of the holes is reduced by approximately 80% compared to the rigid location method of the entire blade, and the average value and standard deviation are also decreased by about 70%

In order to obtain improved performance in terms of combustion eciency and thrust-weight ratio, the turbine inlet temperature (1700–2000 K) has far exceeded the melting point (about 1700 K) of the turbine blade [1]
The lm cooling method is normally suggested to enhance the high-temperature creep resistance and maintain the normal state of the turbine blade [2]

The key to increasing the aero-engine's operational eciency is to correctly machine the lm cooling holes of the turbine blade [3], where two accuracy issues need to be resolved: exact dimension and accurate location
The lm cooling holes have a deep depth and a relatively narrow radius, often between 0
8 mm, which are typical high aspect ratio micro holes, are therefore challenging to produce using traditional techniques [4]

With the development of EDM and ultrashort pulse laser processing technology, as well as the maturity of related experiments, mathematical modelling and other process methods [5][6], the machining error of the micro hole gradually satises the accurate dimensional requirements of roundness, taper, contour and other parameters

However, due to the intricate design and thin-walled structure, the cooling rate of the blade surface varies according to the curvature statues, which inuences the casting process of the turbine blade and causes uneven deformation [7]
